svg.title: Telecom, Waste, and Vendor Audit Gate Check
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-indirect-expense-audit-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Telecom, Waste, and Vendor Audit Gate Check; subtitle: Four gates before an indirect-expense engagement pays out; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does the client spend at least $2,000 a month in one audited category?; pass next: G2; fail action: Park the account; Zog Inc sets $2,000 a month in a category as the point where it is worth the conversation.; gate: G2; question: Is a ledger baseline locked and an inflation cap in place before the term ends?; pass next: G3; fail action: Talk to the current hauler and competing haulers before renewal; Barracuda B2B has seen rates jump as much as 25% at year end with no cap.; gate: G3; question: Is every overfill or overage fee backed by driver photo proof?; pass next: G4; fail action: Back-claim credits; Zog Inc reports Paige clawed back three years of credits on a $25-a-week overfill fee.; gate: G4; question: Are disconnected telecom circuits fully dead, with USF taxes and exemptions checked line by line?; pass next: Contingent savings report to the CFO; fail action: Kill half-disconnected circuits where the modem or NID still bills, per Macronet Services.; caption: Schooley Mitchell practitioners claim 28% average savings since 1998, with 80 percent of recommendations requiring no supplier change. Street wins include a 37% UPS cut on a $400K account by stripping the fuel surcharge and about $370K in Auditel telecom credits.; assumptions note: Gate order follows a spend-first, then contract, then fee-proof, then circuit sequence; practitioners split on DIY versus analyst-led work. Watchdog Advisory reports $25M recovered plus $5M in future workers' comp savings, with lookbacks of five to seven years.; note: Attributed to Zog Inc (u-o74Ze2VNs), Barracuda B2B (vnkFP_2Jzng), Macronet Services (QMubvpeApZk), RiverForest Connections (VvAP-sQig0I), Auditel, Inc. Telecom Expense Management (gIcFGhjFIKI), and Watchdog Advisory (Joo1fuo4HkY).

text.title: Telecom, Waste, and Vendor Audit Gate Check
text.tspan: Telecom, Waste, and Vendor Audit Gate Check

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does the client spend at least $2,000 a month in one audited category?; pass next: G2; fail action: Park the account; Zog Inc sets $2,000 a month in a category as the point where it is worth the conversation.

gate: G2; question: Is a ledger baseline locked and an inflation cap in place before the term ends?; pass next: G3; fail action: Talk to the current hauler and competing haulers before renewal; Barracuda B2B has seen rates jump as much as 25% at year end with no cap.

gate: G3; question: Is every overfill or overage fee backed by driver photo proof?; pass next: G4; fail action: Back-claim credits; Zog Inc reports Paige clawed back three years of credits on a $25-a-week overfill fee.

gate: G4; question: Are disconnected telecom circuits fully dead, with USF taxes and exemptions checked line by line?; pass next: Contingent savings report to the CFO; fail action: Kill half-disconnected circuits where the modem or NID still bills, per Macronet Services.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order follows a spend-first, then contract, then fee-proof, then circuit sequence; practitioners split on DIY versus analyst-led work. Watchdog Advisory reports $25M recovered plus $5M in future workers' comp savings, with lookbacks of five to seven years.
